intro_html: Fasolka po bretonsku is what Polish baked beans actually taste like: smoky bacon and sausage, white beans, tomato, thyme and a lot of smoked paprika, simmered until the whole thing goes thick. It is a genuinely cheap protein per dollar build, landing 27 grams of protein for about $2.79 a bowl (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $2.79 a bowl (at everyday cost). Beans do the heavy lifting, the bacon and sausage do the flavoring, and the result costs less than a soda at a gas station.
shop_smart: Canned white beans are the whole trick. A few cans cost less than any meat you could add and they carry most of the protein and all of the body in this dish. Dried beans are cheaper still if you plan a day ahead.
Bacon and sausage are the two real cost lines. Together they are most of the batch. Buy both on sale and freeze them, because both freeze without any loss.
Tomato paste is the cheapest flavor concentrate in the store. A single small can barely moves the total and it gives this stew the deep tomato backbone that thin sauce cannot.
Smoked paprika, thyme, oregano and bay carry the seasoning. That whole list is jars you already own, which is why the shopping trip stays so short.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon, slice the smoked sausage into coins, dice the onion and mince the garlic. Drain and rinse the beans.
Render the bacon in a heavy pot until the fat runs and the pieces crisp at the edges.
Add the vegetable oil and brown the sausage coins in the bacon fat until they take on color.
Cook the diced onion until soft, then add the garlic and the tomato paste and stir for a couple of minutes so the paste darkens and loses its raw edge.
Stir in the smoked paprika, regular paprika, dried thyme, oregano and bay leaves, then pour in the diced tomatoes and the beef broth.
Add the drained beans and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces and coats the beans instead of pooling around them.
Pull out the bay leaves, season with salt and black pepper, and cook the rice separately to serve underneath.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and ladle the exact amount over rice in each container. Every bowl lands near 590 calories and 27 grams of protein.

steps: Render the chopped bacon until crisp, then brown the sliced sausage in the fat.
Cook the onion until soft, then add garlic and tomato paste and stir until the paste darkens.
Stir in the smoked paprika, paprika, thyme, oregano and bay leaves, then add the diced tomatoes and beef broth.
Add the drained white beans and simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens around them.
Remove the bay leaves, season, and serve over cooked rice.
